<thought>By interpreting the measurements as pairwise equivalent resistances of a tree (since only four resistors can form a connected graph of five nodes), the smallest distance (5 Ω) must be a direct edge N1–X3. Using the other measurements, the unique tree that satisfies all pairwise resistances is:

- B–N3 = 20 Ω  
- N3–N2 = 15 Ω  
- N2–N1 = 10 Ω  
- N1–X3 = 5 Ω  

These four resistors reproduce every given measurement (e.g., B–N2 = 20+15 = 35 Ω, N1–N2 = 10 Ω, etc.). Assigning the labels from left to right gives R1 = 20 Ω, R2 = 15 Ω, R3 = 10 Ω, R4 = 5 Ω.
